title: Outlook: sort a folder's subfolders from A to Z in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web
summary: Hold: the briefing turns a planned user action into unsupported guarantees about whose folder order can change and whether any administrator role is involved. The roadmap dates and scope match, and the cited licensing guidance is accurate, but the assurances about permissions, retention, storage and mail actions also go beyond the published description.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let users sort a folder's subfolders alphabetically from the parent folder.
claims.quote: You'll be able to sort a folder's subfolders alphabetically from the parent folder.

claims.claim: The roadmap says this avoids rearranging subfolders individually and helps organize long folder lists.
claims.quote: This makes it easier to find the folder you need without rearranging subfolders one by one. It's a simple way to keep long folder lists organized.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether this planned sort replaces a custom subfolder order or allows restoration.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z parent folder custom order shared mailboxes sync. Read roadmap, policy-management and results; community discussion of existing sorting does not establish replacement or restoration behavior for this planned feature.

claims.claim: Shared-mailbox and additional-account support for the planned parent-folder sort is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z parent folder custom order shared mailboxes sync. Read roadmap, licensing-options, policy-management and results; none states shared-mailbox or additional-account support for this planned sort.

claims.claim: Persistence and cross-client synchronization of this planned sort order are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z parent folder custom order shared mailboxes sync. Read roadmap, mailFolder reference and results; community reports about existing mobile sorting do not document persistence of this planned feature.

claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders alphabetically licensing price meter; "sort subfolders" "licensing". Opened licensing-options; it describes Outlook product licensing and names no entitlement specific to parent-folder subfolder sorting.

claims.claim: The licensing page publishes no meter or separate charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders alphabetically licensing price meter. Read licensing-options in full; it lists desktop and web/mobile entitlements but no charge or meter for parent-folder sorting.

claims.where: controls[0] (ui and api null); summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator UI or automation control for allowing subfolder A-to-Z sorting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook folder sort order admin policy Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration. Read policy-management, both cmdlet references (searched sort/folder), and Graph mailFolder; none documents this control.

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy has no documented folder-sort-order parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook folder sort order admin policy Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration; searched the fetched Set-OwaMailboxPolicy reference for sort and folder. No sort-order parameter appears.

claims.claim: Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration has no documented folder-sort-order parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook folder sort order admin policy Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration; searched the fetched mailbox-configuration reference for sort and folder. ConversationSortOrder sorts messages, not the folder list.

claims.claim: Most Outlook on the web mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.

claims.claim: A user's folder order changes only when that user sorts, and only users who choose to sort see a change.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z parent folder custom order shared mailboxes sync; Outlook sort subfolders A to Z automatic default permissions retention mail storage. Read roadmap, policy-management and mailFolder; none establishes this exclusive guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of the first Why it matters paragraph with 'The roadmap describes a user-initiated sort from a parent folder.' Replace the impact rationale with 'Low. The roadmap describes an optional sorting action for people managing subfolder lists.' Keep defaultState as user-opt-in; do not claim that only the initiating user can see an order change while synchronization and shared-mailbox behavior remain undocumented.

claims.claim: The change does not touch permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z automatic default permissions retention mail storage. Read roadmap and policy-management; the roadmap describes sorting but does not state that permissions are unaffected.
claims.fix: Replace 'The change does not touch permissions, retention or where mail is stored, as the roadmap describes it.' with 'The roadmap describes subfolder sorting; it does not describe changes to permissions, retention or mail storage.'

claims.claim: The change does not touch retention.

claims.fix: Use the replacement sentence given for the permissions claim: 'The roadmap describes subfolder sorting; it does not describe changes to permissions, retention or mail storage.'

claims.claim: The change does not touch where mail is stored.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z automatic default permissions retention mail storage. Read roadmap and Graph mailFolder reference; neither specifies storage behavior for this planned sort.
claims.fix: Use the replacement sentence given for the permissions claim: 'The roadmap describes subfolder sorting; it does not describe changes to permissions, retention or mail storage.'

claims.claim: Sorting takes no action on mail.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook sort subfolders A to Z automatic default permissions retention mail storage. Read roadmap, policy-management and Graph mailFolder reference; none expressly documents the absence of mail actions for this feature.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: No mail action is described: the roadmap says users will be able to sort a folder's subfolders alphabetically from the parent folder.

claims.claim: No admin role is involved.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook folder sort order admin policy Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration. Read policy-management and both cmdlet references; no feature-specific setting was found, but none states that no admin role is involved.
claims.fix: Remove 'no admin role is involved;' and retain 'Microsoft Learn documents no admin setting for the feature.' An absence of a documented switch does not establish a role requirement or its absence.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says nothing about sign-in, permissions or delegation.
